target_customer: Web3 developers and teams that need on-chain data in their apps, plus compliance and security users
problem: Building and running pipelines that index blocks, events, transactions, wallets and tokens is slow and costly for small Web3 teams.
business_model: Managed data infrastructure with subscription or usage pricing (pricing not found)

founders.name: Adit Patel
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built multiple Web3 projects before Blockscope; details not found.

founders.name: Maharshi Patel
founders.background_notes: Sources conflict on who is the primary founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi-chain indexing and reliable storage of live and historical data is standard but demanding data engineering for a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: Indexing and pipeline tooling was offered by several vendors and open source projects, and no proprietary data or lock-in is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Blockscope; it appears to have stayed small.

market_need_then: The Block reported the Summer 2022 YC batch leaned toward Web3 infrastructure during a bear market, which suggests developer demand for data tooling but weak crypto funding conditions.

branding.domain_note: Uses blockscope.co rather than the .com, per LinkedIn and the YC page.

identity.logo: A logo exists on aggregator pages but no description was retrievable
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline from YC launch post: Easy to use crypto tools for all.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or merch about the brand was found; search results confused it with Blocknative and Blockscout.

outcome_analysis: Blockscope remains listed as active with four people and no public acquisition, shutdown or layoff news. It joined YC in Summer 2022 as crypto funding cooled, and no later financing, customer wins or product milestones were found. Its trajectory is therefore unknown rather than a clear success or failure.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and VCBacked, both aggregators, report about 500K USD total from YC in Aug or Sep 2022 (they disagree on date and instrument); not recorded as a round. Creative Destruction Lab appears as a possible backer on CB Insights only. Location conflicts (YC says Toronto, aggregators say New York, San Francisco or Singapore). No dated competitor sources near July 2022 were found, so the list is empty; later comparison pages name Dune, Nansen, Covalent and The Graph. Company website fetch returned only the page title. Completeness pass: the 500K convertible note dated 2022-09-07 rests on a single database (CB Insights); VCBacked calls it a pre seed dated August 2022.
